claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a narrow basis despite a known 1.1-point performance gap in the clinical-trial intake segment, because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the gap can be handled through explicit documentation and ongoing monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Product claims that the segment is non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when customer commitments name the segment.
For a material limitation, certification is supportable only if the issue is resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
General public guidance on monitoring and documentation can support controls, but cannot substitute for the specific internal policy requirement.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the clinical-trial intake gap must be disclosed before launch.
The actual model-card or launch disclosure showing this limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if the limitation was not resolved before launch.
Any launch-governance approval explicitly addressing the named hospital pilot commitments and this gap.
specific_concerns: The affected segment is a named launch use case and appears material under the stated policy.
The policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Available evidence shows legal review on disclosure is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
Public guidance on monitoring and model-card documentation supports process discipline, but does not itself authorize certification under the enterprise policy.
The actor's packet narrows the justification appropriately, but still overreaches by treating certification as supportable without evidence that disclosure or approved risk acceptance is complete.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant under policy.
That documenting the gap and monitoring it is sufficient absent evidence of completed disclosure or approved pre-launch risk acceptance.
Any implication that the materiality issue is already resolved.
